Membranous nephropathy: 3

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

An adult with a compatible nephrotic presentation has circulating antibodies to the phospholipase A2 receptor. Which disease mechanism is supported by this result, interpreted with the rest of the clinical assessment?

  1. Near-normal glomeruli on light microscopy
  2. No substantial immune deposits on immunofluorescence
  3. Frequent corticosteroid responsiveness in typical childhood disease
  4. Anti-PLA2R-associated autoimmunity
  5. Podocyte foot-process effacement
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Anti-PLA2R-associated autoimmunity

Anti-PLA2R antibodies support PLA2R-associated membranous nephropathy in the appropriate clinical context.

Understanding the options

Anti-PLA2R-associated autoimmunity
Anti-PLA2R antibodies support PLA2R-associated membranous nephropathy in the appropriate clinical context.
Podocyte foot-process effacement
Electron microscopy detects loss of normal podocyte foot-process architecture in many proteinuric diseases. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Near-normal glomeruli on light microscopy
Minimal change disease can have striking proteinuria despite little visible light-microscopic change. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
No substantial immune deposits on immunofluorescence
Classic minimal change disease lacks the immune-complex staining pattern of membranous nephropathy. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Frequent corticosteroid responsiveness in typical childhood disease
Typical childhood minimal change disease often responds to corticosteroids; atypical or resistant cases require reassessment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
